checks.name: The launch is recorded: host, runtime process and its start time, ports
The host is killed: its runtime and database keep running, the record remains
The next launch reclaims both by the record, starts again and serves the same library; writing works
A clean quit leaves nothing to reclaim

limits: One machine, one run. The host is ended with SIGKILL while idle; a kill in the middle of a write is not produced here. POSIX process groups only: the Windows path (taskkill on the recorded process tree) is written and not rehearsed.
